messages.subject: finite diffs test (applied to Wishart sampler)
parts:
Matt was right (does that go without saying
at this point?). The finite diff calcs are
very useful.

I refactored his code in prob_grad.hpp a bit
so that the finite diff calc is separated from
the test and there are some random inits. It
should be separated even further into a math
lib at some point as we discussed earlier.

I also removed the printf (welcome to the C++
era). Matt's function still works as is after
the refactoring.

I also put a flag --test_grad into the model so
that a compiled Stan model can be put
into "gradient test mode" which validates the
model's gradient calc with finite differences.
Here's an example.

~/stan> demo/wish --test_grad

param k model finite diff error
0 0 -5.00044e-07 5.00044e-07
1 0 -5.00044e-07 5.00044e-07
2 0 0 0
3 1.5 1.5 5.00279e-07
4 1 0.999999 1.00017e-06
5 0 -2.00018e-06 2.00018e-06

So gradients look OK for the Wishart.

I need to clean this up a bit to use the same
inits as specified in the model, but that's trivial.

That still only tests at the initial point.
I could also do what I think Matt was intending and run
the test at every leapfrog step. But then I'm not
sure I want to print out so agressively in that case.
I can also clean up the prints so that they're in
scientific notation in every case so they're easier
to compare by eye.

- Bob
